<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|318|THE ACTES|CHA. X.}}</noinclude>vnto Ioppé, and call hither one Simon that is surnamed Peter. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=6}}† he lodgeth vvith one Simon a tanner, vvhose house is by the sea side. he vvil tel thee vvhat thou must doe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=7}}† And vvhen the Angel vvas departed that spake to him, he called tvvo of his houshold, and a souldiar that feared our Lord, of them that vvere vnder him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=8}}† To vvhom vvhen he had told all, he sent them vnto Ioppé.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=9}}† And the next day vvhiles they vvere going on their iourney, and dravving nigh to the citie, Peter vvent vp into the higher partes, {{sup|‖}} to pray about the sixt houre. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=10}}† And being hungrie, he vvas desirous to take somevvhat. And as they vvere preparing, there fel vpon him an excesse of minde: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=11}}† and he savv the heauen opened, and a certaine vessel descending, as it vvere a great linnen sheete vvith foure corners let dovvne from heauen to the earth, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=12}}† vvherein vvere al foure-footed beastes, and that creepe on the earth, and foules of the aire. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=13}}† And there came a voice to him, Arise Peter: kil, and eate. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=14}}† But Peter said, God forbid, Lord: for I did neuer eate any common and vncleane thing. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=15}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Here God first vttered to Peter that the time vvas come to preach also to the Gentiles, and to cõuerse vvith them for their saluation, no lesse then vvith the Ievves, vvith ful freedõ to eate al meates vvithout respecte of the prohibition of certaine, made in the old Law.}}∷ a voice came to him againe the second time, That vvhich God hath purified, doe not thou cal common. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=16}}† And this vvas done thrise. and forthvvith the vessel was taken vp againe into heauen. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=17}}† And vvhiles Peter doubted vvithin him self, vvhat the vision should be that he had seen, behold the men that vvere sent from Cornelius, inquiring for Simons house, stood at the gate. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=18}}† And vvhen they had called, they asked, if Simon that is surnamed Peter, vvere lodged there. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=19}}† And as Peter vvas thinking of the vision, the Spirit said to him, Behold three men doe seeke thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=20}}† Arise therfore, and get thee dovvne, and goe vvith them, doubting nothing: for I haue sent them. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=21}}† And Peter going dovvne to the men, said, Behold, I am he vvhom you seeke: vvhat is the cause, for the vvhich you are come? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=22}}† Vvho said, Cornelius the Centurion, a iust man & that feareth God, and hauing testimonie of al the nation of the Ievves, receiued an ansvver of an holy Angel to send for thee into his house, and to heare vvordes of thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=23}}† Therfore bringing them in, he lodged them.

And the day folovving he arose and vvent vvith them: and certaine of the brethren of Ioppé accompanied him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=24}}† And on the morow he entred into Cæsaréa. And Cornelius expected them, hauing called together his kinne, and special<noinclude>{{rh|||frendes.}}</noinclude>
